description:
Integration tests covering the encryption invariants. Independent oracles throughout — no test may use the encryption code as its own oracle.

## Test cases

  ### FieldCipher (unit, OpenSSL oracle)
  1. Known plaintext + known DEK → known ciphertext (cross-validated with OpenSSL)
  2. Tampered ciphertext (flip one byte) → Err, not wrong plaintext
  3. Empty plaintext → valid ciphertext → decrypts to empty
  4. Two encryptions of same plaintext with same DEK → DIFFERENT ciphertexts (nonce is random)

  ### UserKeyStore (integration, two-call oracle)
  5. get_dek called twice → same plaintext DEK returned (DEK is stable)
  6. destroy_dek then get_dek → KeyServiceError::InvalidKey or equivalent
  7. ON DELETE CASCADE: delete users row → user_encryption_keys row gone

  ### Message encryption (integration, direct DB query oracle)
  8. Store message, query DB directly → raw_message column is NOT the original plaintext
     (i.e., the DB never sees plaintext — verified by raw SQL, not through the app layer)
  9. Store message as user A, attempt decrypt with user B DEK → CipherError
  10. Store message, retrieve via Email/get → returns original plaintext

  ### Erasure (integration)
  11. Store message, delete user, attempt decrypt → error
  12. After deletion, messages row still exists (DB bytes persist, but are unreadable)

## Oracle discipline
  Tests 8 and 9 require bypassing the app layer to query the DB directly.
  Use sqlx::query_scalar to fetch the raw bytes and assert they do NOT match
  the expected plaintext. This is the independent oracle — the app layer
  cannot be used to verify that the app layer is encrypting.
title: Tests: DEK roundtrip, cross-user isolation, and erasure guarantee
